title.narrative: 3a: At least 1500 NAF beneficiaries are trained in employability, vocational and entrepreneurial skills programmes. (Year 3 2023)

description.narrative: Indicative date of completion: 4th Quarter 2023Source(s) of verification: Sajjil databaseExpected date of transmission to the Commission: 1st Quarter 2024Amount attached: EUR 1,500,000Department in charge: Ministry of LabourIn line with the Economic Empowerment Program for the Poor and Vulnerable developed by NAF and MoL, the National Employment Platform (Sajjil) is being upgraded. Employment support will be open to all job seekers but only selected individuals from households in the NAF Takaful 1 database (the target population) will have access to certain subsidised support programs.Selection criteria (using NAF database):Households who are closer to the poverty line as proxied by Takaful 1 eligibility threshold;One person per each household;1840 years old with basic education, able to work but unemployed or working informally;Priority to be given to the head of the household. Once registered in the Sajjil database, the labour market readiness of the jobseekers is assessed. A statistical approach has been developed to classify them into 3 types:1.Market ready;2.Near market ready;3.Hard to place.Near market ready and hard to place job seekers will be referred to employment offices (EO) where officers develop customized action plans and refer the jobseekers to different programs. NAF beneficiaries will largely fall under the hard to place and the near market ready category. Considering the timeframe and the investment needed, for this indicator the focus will be on near market ready jobseekers.

Employment support will be open to all job seekers but only selected individuals from households in the NAF Takaful 1 database (the target population) will have access to certain subsidised support programs.Selection criteria (using NAF database):Households who are closer to the poverty line as proxied by Takaful 1 eligibility threshold;One person per each household;1840 years old with basic education, able to work but unemployed or working informally;Priority to be given to the head of the household. Once registered in the Sajjil database, the labour market readiness of the jobseekers is assessed. A statistical approach has been developed to classify them into 3 types:1.Market ready;2.Near market ready;3.Hard to place.Near market ready and hard to place job seekers will be referred to employment offices (EO) where officers develop customized action plans and refer the jobseekers to different programs. NAF beneficiaries will largely fall under the hard to place and the near market ready category. Considering the timeframe and the investment needed, for this indicator the focus will be on near market ready jobseekers.
